meta.notes: 9-week post-White River rebuild to Vermont 50K (Sun 9/27: 32-33 mi, ~5,600 ft as 20+ repeated climbs/descents, 37% gravel road, NO POLES). PHASES: W1-2 recovery-dominant (walk/run rebuild, symptom-gated), W3-6 Build, W7 Peak, W8 Taper, W9 Race week. WEEKLY SKELETON (W3+): Mon rest / Tue hill intervals + PM Lower A / Wed easy + upper / Thu easy w-descent block + PM Lower B / Fri easy + strides or gear-change pickups / Sat shakeout + upper / SUN LONG RUN (moved to Sunday to match race day). Run before strength on every double day; no lower-body strength day-of or day-before the long run. PRIORITY MAP: P1 tendon durability lives in the strength plan and daily routines; P2 hill intervals (pole-free, absorbs runnable-grade economy) from W3; P3 descent capacity gated — Gate 1 (PT assessment) CLEARED pre-plan, gentle exposure from W3, Gate 2 descent-calibration session W5 Thursday clears race-specific volume from W6. INTENSITY DECISION (coach-owned, resolved): hill intervals Z3-capped per the validated HR-led model; plus short 15-20s uphill strides from W3 — alactic, low-eccentric, targeting the +4..8% cadence-collapse finding; strides are the first thing pulled on any lateral-ankle symptom. No sustained Z4+ work this cycle. LOAD-PATTERN GUARD (June injury lesson): long runs on ROLLING RUNNABLE terrain (100-150 ft/mi, gravel/dirt ideal), never technical-descent mountain routes; min 6 days between long runs; RAMP GUARD (rev 1.2 — rewritten per Race_Strategy_Response_v1 Answers A1/A2/A3). DENOMINATOR: the guard is enforced against SUMMED SESSIONS, never against weekly_targets. weekly_targets.mileage_mi and .vertical_ft are DERIVED fields regenerated from each week's own session sums; they must never be hand-authored, and any loader should assert equality within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. Rationale: the guard protects tissue, and tissue experiences what is prescribed, not what is summarized. RULES: (1) the W2->W3 step is the recovery-exit rebuild and is exempt from BOTH the percentage and the absolute caps — on session sums it is +9.5 mi / +2,150 ft (14.5 -> 24.0 mi, 300 -> 2,450 ft), roughly double what the old header view (12 -> 19 mi) implied, and it REQUIRES EXPLICIT COACH SIGN-OFF before Week 3 begins; it is not approved by default. (2) absolute caps of +5 mi AND +500 ft apply to any ramp BEGINNING from a week whose session-summed mileage is <=30 mi — the STARTING week is the test. (3) once the starting week exceeds 30 mi the cap is 10%, applied SEPARATELY to mileage and to vertical, each against its own prior-week session sum. (4) any breach pauses the progression at the prior week's volume and flags the coach. COMPLIANCE AT REV 1.2, all on session sums: W3->W4 +5.0 mi / +500 ft (at cap, compliant); W4->W5 +5.0 mi / +500 ft (at cap, compliant); W5->W6 +8.8% mi / +8.7% ft (compliant); W6->W7 +8.1% mi / +9.3% ft (compliant); W7->W8 and W8->W9 both decrease. No breaches. HEADROOM WARNING: the vertical ladder now runs at 87-100% of its ceiling in every build week, and W4 and W5 sit EXACTLY at +500 ft. There is no spare vertical anywhere in W4-W7. Adding gain to any session — including route substitutions that happen to climb more — breaks compliance downstream. The B1 rehearsal spec consumed the last of the headroom; any further vertical request must be funded by an explicit trim elsewhere, not absorbed. W2->W3 EXEMPTION — SETTLED RULE (Run_Plan_rev1_2_Verification_Memo section 3, no longer provisional): the exemption covers BOTH the percentage and the absolute caps. Rationale: the ramp guard is a build-phase instrument, and W2 is a symptom-gated walk/run rebuild whose session sums are not load-comparable to run weeks — walk miles are not run miles — so no arithmetic rule spanning W2->W3 is meaningful in either direction. Governance of that step belongs to the three symptom gates plus the conditional sign-off below, not to the ladder. No re-solve is triggered by this ruling. W2->W3 CONDITIONAL SIGN-OFF (athlete-set, closes the last open human item): the step is PRE-APPROVED AT FULL SIZE (+9.5 mi / +2,150 ft on session sums, 14.5 -> 24.0 mi and 300 -> 2,450 ft) IF AND ONLY IF Weeks 1 and 2 clear all three symptom gates — right lateral ankle, left outer knee, right forefoot — with NO flags. Clean gates means Week 3 starts as written, no further approval needed. ANY flag in W1 or W2 voids the pre-approval, and the ladder re-solves downward with the B1 rehearsal reverting to its 2,600 ft profile (the coupling is stated in the rev 1.2 cover note section 5). Note that a flag severe enough to trigger the existing W1-W2 reset rule is governed by that rule first — reset to the Week 1 Friday level and message the coach — and only then does the reduced-ladder branch apply to whatever Week 3 becomes. LADDER SLACK, computed so the re-solve is not improvised under symptom pressure: holding the 40.0 mi peak week, the W3 floor is 23.06 mi. Against the prescribed 24.0 that is only 0.94 mi of slack — the MILEAGE ladder is effectively rigid, and any meaningful reduction at W3 pulls the peak week down proportionally rather than being absorbed. Vertical is different: the W3 floor is 2,388 ft with the B1 spec intact (62 ft of slack) but 2,058 ft once the rehearsal reverts to 2,600 (392 ft of slack). So the reverted branch buys vertical room and almost no mileage room. Anyone re-solving this ladder should size W3 first, then let W4-W7 fall out of the caps, and expect the peak week to shrink with it; any two of (long run, descent session, steep hill session) never on consecutive days. RECALIBRATION CHECKPOINT W5: Thursday Gate 2 descent session + Sunday rolling calibration long run, both recorded clean and FIT files sent to the Race Strategy project for the Vermont pacing plan v1. Addendum A June-13 tables are CEILINGS from peak fitness — context only, not current targets; the W5 calibration supersedes them. HR ZONES at LTHR 168 — CORRECTED CONTIGUOUS TABLE (per HR_Zone_Gap_Report_v1; orphan bpm values 150/158/167 assigned to their nearest percentage boundary): Z1 Recovery <142 | Z2 Aerobic 142-150 | Z3 Tempo 151-158 | Z4 Sub-threshold 159-167 | Z5a Threshold 168-171. Z5b/c undefined by design — nothing in this program operates there. Nothing operational moves: first-10-mi cap 149 (inside Z2), descent throttle 152 (low Z3), never-cross 158 (now cleanly top of Z3). FIELD CONVENTION: hr_zone = INTENDED EXECUTION BAND (range labels like Z1-2/Z2-3 allowed where intent spans a boundary); hr_cap_bpm = HARD CEILING / alarm value, which may sit above the intended band as a declared tripwire. DOWNSTREAM: whoever parses the Week-5 calibration FIT files (8/27 Gate 2 + 8/30 long run) must bucket HR with these same zone edges (150 in Z2, 158 in Z3) — flag in the parser workflow before processing, not after. SYMPTOM GATES throughout: right lateral-ankle tendon (unproven under load), left outer knee, right forefoot — any recurrence pauses descent work and strides, flags the coach. WEEKLY VERTICAL COMPLIANCE CHECK (added rev 1.3 per verification memo section 4): the Sunday compliance check is extended beyond session completion. Each Sunday, compare ACTUAL GPS-measured weekly vertical against that week's derived weekly_targets.vertical_ft. Because the vertical ladder runs at 87-100% of its ceiling in every build week (W4 and W5 sit exactly at +500 ft), a route substitution that climbs 200 ft over plan is a guard breach, not a rounding difference — the check must catch it the week it happens, not at the next review. Over by more than ~100 ft: the following week's ceiling recomputes off the ACTUAL sum, not the plan, and the coach is messaged. This applies with full force to the two calibration days (8/27 Gate 2 and 8/30 long run), where planned-vs-actual is also checked on the Race Strategy side when the FIT files arrive.
meta.revision_notes: rev 1.3 (2026-07-27): closes Run_Plan_rev1_2_Verification_Memo. Section 3 ruling adopted — the W2->W3 exemption covers both the percentage and the absolute caps as a settled rule; the open-ambiguity language is removed. Athlete-set CONDITIONAL SIGN-OFF written in: W2->W3 is pre-approved at full size if Weeks 1-2 clear all three symptom gates with no flags; any flag voids it and re-solves the ladder downward with the B1 rehearsal reverting to 2,600 ft. Ladder slack pre-computed (W3 floor 23.06 mi; 2,388 ft spec-intact / 2,058 ft reverted) so the re-solve is not improvised mid-block. Section 4 addition implemented: Sunday compliance check extended to actual GPS vertical vs derived header, with a >100 ft overage recomputing the next week's ceiling off actual. Section 1 cosmetic footnote fixed: explicit elevation_gain_ft: 0 written to all shakeout and walk sessions that previously omitted the field, and the 'absent = 0' convention added to every derivation_rule. No session loads changed; the ladder, the guard compliance result and the B1 rehearsal spec are identical to rev 1.2. Strength and nutrition plans UNCHANGED.

exercises.name: Walking knee hugs
exercises.cue: Pull knee to chest, balance on standing leg for 1 second.

exercises.name: Leg swings — front/back
exercises.cue: Hold something for balance; relaxed, full range.

exercises.name: Leg swings — side/side
exercises.cue: Open the hip, don't twist the spine.

exercises.name: Walking lunges
exercises.cue: Front knee tracks over second toe; keep torso tall.

exercises.name: Glute bridges
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes at the top; ribs down.

exercises.name: High knees
exercises.cue: Quick turnover; emphasize lift, not speed.

exercises.name: Strides (quality days only)
exercises.cue: Build to ~85% of 5K pace over 20 sec. 60 sec full recovery between. Skip on easy days.

pre_run.notes: Do this BEFORE every run. On easy/shakeout days, omit strides. On quality days (hill intervals, race-rhythm sessions), include the 3 x strides. During recovery weeks 1-2, do the mobility items only, gently.

exercises.name: Walking cooldown
exercises.cue: Walk until HR is below 110 bpm before stretching.

exercises.name: Standing quad stretch
exercises.cue: Tuck pelvis under to feel the stretch in the front of the hip too.

exercises.name: Standing calf stretch (bent + straight knee)
exercises.cue: Two angles per side: knee straight (gastroc) and knee bent (soleus).

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Squeeze the back glute first, THEN lean forward.

exercises.name: Pigeon stretch
exercises.cue: Square hips. If knee complains, lie back instead (figure-4 supine).

exercises.name: Foam roll quads, IT band, calves (optional)
exercises.cue: 60 seconds per area; pause and breathe on tender spots.

post_run.notes: Do within 15 minutes of finishing the run. Especially important after long runs and power-climb days — eccentric load + walking cooldown protects the quads.

weekly_targets.notes: Recovery week 1 of 2. Walking only until Friday; first jog steps are symptom-gated. Mileage figure counts jogged minutes only. SYMPTOM GATE all week: any sharp or localized pain in the right lateral ankle, left outer knee, or right forefoot ends the session and pushes the progression back 2 days.
weekly_targets.derivation_rule: DERIVED FIELD — regenerated from this week's session sums (race excluded). Never hand-author. Loaders should assert mileage_mi and vertical_ft equal the session sums within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. W1 EXCEPTION: Week 1 sessions are duration-prescribed walk/jog with no distance or vertical values, so the derived header is 0 by construction. Actual content is ~175 min of walking with ~14 min of jogged intervals. The pre-rev-1.2 header of "3 mi" was a hand-authored estimate of jogged minutes and has been removed rather than fabricated back. LOADER CONVENTION: a session omitting elevation_gain_ft or distance_mi is treated as 0; as of rev 1.3 all such fields are written explicitly, so an absent field now indicates a malformed record rather than a zero.

weeks.week_notes: Days 2-8 post-White River. The job this week is circulation and tissue protection, not fitness. Elevation and gentle walking early; short jog intervals only from Friday, only if walking is fully comfortable. No NSAIDs around any loading (blunts collagen remodeling). Strength plan carries the P1 tendon-entry work (isometrics, no HSR).

days.day_notes: Full rest. Short walks around the house, elevation when sitting, pre-stand mobility. Day 2 post-race.

sessions.title: Recovery walk
sessions.key_cue: Flat, supportive shoes, conversational stroll. This is circulation, not training.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Walk only. Note how the right lateral ankle and left knee feel at the start vs. end — this is baseline data for the week.

sessions.title: Recovery walk
sessions.key_cue: Slightly longer. Still flat. Stop early without guilt if anything localizes.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Tendon-entry strength session this evening (see strength plan) — isometrics only.

days.day_notes: Rest from walking volume. Daily routines + evening isometrics only. Assess: is walking symptom-free? That answer gates Friday.

sessions.title: Walk + first jog steps (gated)
sessions.key_cue: 6 x 1 min VERY easy jog inside a 45-min walk — ONLY if walking has been fully symptom-free since Wednesday.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Day 6 post-race. If any of the three sites (right lateral ankle, left outer knee, right forefoot) speaks up on the jog steps, drop back to walking and retry Sunday.

days.day_notes: Rest or optional 25-30 min flat walk. Flex day — listen to the legs.

sessions.title: Long walk + jog intervals
sessions.key_cue: 8 x 1 min easy jog inside a 60-min walk if Friday was clean. Gentle terrain OK, nothing steep or technical.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. End-of-week checkpoint: report symptom status — it sets Week 2's walk/run ratios.

weekly_targets.notes: Recovery week 2 of 2. Walk/run progressing toward continuous easy running by Saturday. Still no HSR in the gym, still flat/gentle terrain, still symptom-gated. Target ~12 mi combined walk+run.

weeks.week_notes: Rebuild week. The pre-race walk/run protocol proved this pathway works — same structure, faster timeline because there is no acute injury, only post-race tissue caution. By Sunday the goal is ~70 min mostly-running. Any regression at the three sites resets to Week 1 Friday level and flags a message to the coach. DECISION POINT AT WEEK'S END (rev 1.3): the W2->W3 step is pre-approved at full size ONLY if Weeks 1 and 2 clear all three symptom gates with no flags. Review the two weeks on Sunday 8/9 before Week 3 starts. Clean = Week 3 runs exactly as written, no further approval needed. Any flag = the pre-approval is void, the ladder re-solves downward, and the 9/13 rehearsal reverts to its 2,600 ft profile. This is the last open human item in the package; everything else is verified and accepted.

days.day_notes: Rest. Daily routines + evening isometrics.

sessions.title: Walk/run 2:2
sessions.key_cue: 2 min easy run / 2 min walk x 10. Flat. Cadence relaxed, no watch-chasing.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. First structured run/walk. Tendon-entry lower session this evening.

sessions.title: Recovery walk
sessions.key_cue: Pure walk between run/walk days.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Upper strength this evening if energy is normal.

sessions.title: Walk/run 4:2
sessions.key_cue: 4 min easy run / 2 min walk x 7-8. Gentle rolling OK, avoid sustained descent.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Second tendon-entry lower session this evening. 48h from Tuesday's.

days.day_notes: Rest.

sessions.title: First continuous run
sessions.key_cue: 25 min continuous easy. Flat. Stop at 25 even if it feels great — it should feel great.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Milestone session: first continuous run post-race.

sessions.title: Rebuild long walk/run
sessions.key_cue: Mostly easy running with a 2-min walk break every 15 min. Rolling non-technical trail or gravel.
sessions.fueling_notes: Bring 1 gel + water; practice taking it at 30 min even on a short effort — keeps the habit warm.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. End of recovery block. Clean execution here opens the Build phase: hills return Tuesday.

weekly_targets.notes: Build opens. First hill intervals (short, sub-threshold), first descent skill block (gentle, Gate 1 cleared), first strides. 4th strength session added. Ramp guard: nothing this week exceeds 60% of peak-week session sizes. SUNDAY VERTICAL CHECK (rev 1.3): compare actual GPS weekly vertical against this week's derived vertical_ft. Over by more than ~100 ft, next week's ceiling recomputes off the actual sum and the coach is messaged. There is no spare vertical in the ladder.

weeks.week_notes: The 9-week shape starts here: Tue hill intervals + PM Lower A (hill strength), Wed easy + upper, Thu easy with descent block + PM Lower B (tendon HSR begins), Fri easy + strides, Sat shakeout/rest + upper, Sun rolling long. INTENSITY MODEL for the block: hill intervals are Z3-capped (the validated HR-led model); short uphill strides (15-20 s) are the only faster work — alactic, low-eccentric, aimed at the +4..8% gait-collapse finding. Strides are pulled first if the lateral ankle objects. ENTRY CONDITION (rev 1.3): this week is conditional on Weeks 1-2 clearing all three symptom gates with no flags. It is the largest single step in the block (+9.5 mi / +2,150 ft on session sums) and is exempt from the ramp guard by settled rule — which means the symptom gates, not arithmetic, are what protect it. If the gates were not clean, do not start this week as written.

days.day_notes: Rest. Post-long-run recovery slot for the rest of the plan.

sessions.title: Hill intervals — intro
sessions.key_cue: 6 x 90 s RUNNING at +5..8% grade, HR under 155, walk-down recovery. Cadence over 130 on every rep — running, not power-hiking.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Quality. P2 opens. The point is gait, not effort: stay running at grades where the June data shows the cadence collapse (+4..8%). Reps are short on purpose. No poles — the whole cycle is pole-free.

days.day_notes: DOUBLE DAY — AM hills + PM Lower A (hill strength). Run first.

sessions.title: Easy Z2
sessions.key_cue: Conversational. Nose-breathing test on the flats.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy. Upper A this evening. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard on the nominated denominator. Easy-day volume only; the session's purpose is unchanged.

sessions.title: Easy + descent skill block
sessions.key_cue: Within an easy run: 2 x 0.5 mi at -3..5%, RELAXED running, cadence 170+, quiet feet. Non-technical surface.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy + skill. P3 opens gently — Gate 1 is cleared, so moderate-grade descent running begins as the tendon-rebuild medium itself. This is form practice, not load. Lower B (tendon HSR) this evening.

days.day_notes: DOUBLE DAY — AM easy/descent + PM Lower B. Run first.

sessions.title: Easy + first hill strides
sessions.key_cue: 4 x 15 s uphill strides at the end — smooth build to fast-but-relaxed, walk back down. Full recovery.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy + strides. Strides gate: only if the week has been symptom-free at the ankle. These are neuromuscular, not cardio — HR is irrelevant on a 15-s rep. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard on the nominated denominator. Easy-day volume only; the session's purpose is unchanged.

days.day_notes: Rest (or optional 20 min shakeout). Upper B this evening — upper is fine the day before a long run.

sessions.title: Rolling long run
sessions.key_cue: Rolling runnable terrain, ~100 ft/mi. RUN everything up to ~8% — walking is a choice, not a default. Hike only the genuinely steep.
sessions.fueling_notes: Race-cadence habit: gel every 30 min, SaltStick at 45 min, ~500 ml/hr.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Long Z2. Vermont-shaped from day one: gravel/dirt rolling routes, NOT the technical-descent mountain routes that produced the June injury. Load-pattern guard is active for the whole block: no technical 20+ milers, minimum 6 days between long runs, terrain rotated.

weekly_targets.notes: Volume +~25% on a clean Week 3. Hill reps lengthen to 3 min. Descent blocks grow. Gear-change pickups start Friday (the +2..4% running economy work). SUNDAY VERTICAL CHECK (rev 1.3): compare actual GPS weekly vertical against this week's derived vertical_ft. Over by more than ~100 ft, next week's ceiling recomputes off the actual sum and the coach is messaged. There is no spare vertical in the ladder.

weeks.week_notes: Second build week. Everything progresses one notch. Watch the cumulative-fatigue signal on Thursday descents — that is the Vermont-relevant read.

sessions.title: Hill intervals — 3 min reps
sessions.key_cue: 5 x 3 min at +5..8%, Z3 cap 157, jog-down or rolling recovery. Cadence 130+. Finish with 4 x 20 s hill strides.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Quality. Reps now long enough to demand rhythm, still capped at Z3 — race day never needs more, the stimulus is economy and gait. Lower A this evening.

days.day_notes: DOUBLE DAY — AM hills + PM Lower A.

sessions.title: Easy Z2
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy. Upper A this evening. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard on the nominated denominator. Easy-day volume only; the session's purpose is unchanged.

sessions.title: Easy + descent blocks
sessions.key_cue: 3 x 0.75 mi at -4..6%, cadence 170+, controlled but genuinely RUNNING. Non-technical.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy + skill. Descent dose grows. Note any lateral-ankle or lateral-knee feedback within 24h — that is the progression signal, not just in-session feel. Lower B this evening.

days.day_notes: DOUBLE DAY — AM easy/descent + PM Lower B.

sessions.title: Easy + gear-change pickups
sessions.key_cue: 6 x 1 min RUNNING at +2..4% inside the run, cadence 140+, easy jog between. Smooth, tall, quick feet.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy + economy. This is the +2..5% band work: at peak fitness you ran it at 13:31 / cadence 138 — the pickups keep that gait pattern rehearsed while volume rebuilds. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard on the nominated denominator. Easy-day volume only; the session's purpose is unchanged.

sessions.title: Shakeout
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Upper B this evening. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard on the nominated denominator. Easy-day volume only; the session's purpose is unchanged.

sessions.title: Rolling long run
sessions.key_cue: ~110-130 ft/mi rolling. Run-everything intent. Practice the transition rhythm: no settling — every crest changes gear.
sessions.fueling_notes: Gel every 30 min, SaltStick 1/45 min, 500-600 ml/hr.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Long Z2. Vermont is constant gear changes; long runs train the rhythm as much as the legs.

weeks.week_notes: Checkpoint week per the cover note. Gate 2 (descent calibration) sits Thursday: it clears the ramp to race-specific descent volume AND produces the grade-banded descent data. Sunday's long run is the rolling-terrain calibration. Both need clean GPS recording (no pauses mid-effort) and the established parser workflow afterwards. GATE 2 FAIL BRANCH (covers the Sunday calibration run): if Gate 2 flags — symptom escalation at ankle/knee within 24 h — then Sunday 8/30 DROPS to a flat/gentle 10-12 mi easy run WITHOUT calibration status; the calibration long run reschedules to Sunday 9/6 (swapping with the W6 long run), and the coach is messaged before either run happens. Rationale: (1) load — a symptomatic ankle/knee does not get a 16-mi rolling run 72 h later; (2) data — a protective-state FIT file must never feed the Vermont pacing plan (the White River race-matrix lesson). Pacing-plan delivery slips ~1 week in this branch — acceptable, still ~2.5 weeks pre-race.

sessions.title: Hill intervals — back-to-back sets
sessions.key_cue: 6 x 3 min at +5..8% in PAIRS with only a short rolling recovery inside each pair; full jog recovery between pairs. Plus 2 x 30 s strong at +12..15%. Finish 4 x 20 s strides.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Quality. Back-to-back pairs train the Vermont transition rhythm — climb, crest, roll, climb again. The two steep reps cover the brief 12-15% pitches the course profile hides. Lower A this evening.

days.day_notes: DOUBLE DAY — AM hills + PM Lower A.

sessions.title: Easy Z2
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy. Upper A this evening. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard on the nominated denominator. Easy-day volume only; the session's purpose is unchanged.

sessions.title: GATE 2 — Descent calibration session
sessions.key_cue: After 15 min warmup: 2 x 1.5 mi SUSTAINED running at -5..8%, cadence 170+, controlled-strong effort, full recovery between. Non-technical surface. Clean FIT recording.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Calibration/Quality. THE GATE 2 SESSION, deferred from last cycle. Pass criteria: both reps completed at cadence 170+, no symptom escalation at ankle/knee within 24h. Pass clears race-specific descent volume from Week 6. The FIT file goes to the Race Strategy project. Reference ceiling for context, not target: June 13 held 10:38/mi at HR 147 over 6.67 mi of this band. Lower B this evening — tendon work, moderate load given the hard morning. CAP RATIONALE: the 152 cap is the White River descent-throttle signal, correctly inherited — a declared tripwire at low Z3 over an intended Z2 execution band. The intended band is stated unambiguously here because this session's FIT file feeds the Vermont pacing plan. FAIL BRANCH: a flag here also demotes Sunday 8/30 to a flat/gentle 10-12 mi easy (no calibration status) and moves the calibration long run to 9/6 — see week notes.

days.day_notes: DOUBLE DAY — AM Gate 2 descent session + PM Lower B (moderate).

sessions.title: Recovery easy
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Genuinely easy between the two calibration efforts. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard on the nominated denominator. Easy-day volume only; the session's purpose is unchanged.

sessions.title: CALIBRATION rolling long run
sessions.key_cue: Rolling runnable, ~120 ft/mi, run-everything. Steady clean recording, minimal stops. This is the Vermont fitness snapshot.

sessions.title: PEAK long run — Vermont dress rehearsal (S1-S5 spec)
sessions.key_cue: S1 FINAL 8 MILES at >=150 ft/mi (>=1,200 ft between mi 12 and 20). S2 MARQUEE CLIMB at mi 17-18: 1.0-1.2 mi at 6-8%, gaining ~350-400 ft — matched to the race's mi-29.4 Blood Hill climb, not a generic hill. S3 SETUP: the marquee climb must be preceded by 1.5-2.5 mi of sustained RUNNABLE descent at ~4-6%. The descend-then-climb sequence IS the rehearsal — an average-density day cannot reproduce it. S4 DAY TOTAL ~3,000 ft (~150 ft/mi); front half stays at the gentler current density to control total eccentric load. S5 Time the caffeine gel so the marquee climb arrives 15-20 min after it, mirroring the race-day rule.
sessions.fueling_notes: FULL RACE DRESS REHEARSAL — see nutrition date override 2026-09-13. Practice caffeine-gel timing in the final 90 min.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Long Z2 / dress rehearsal. Rehearses the whole race day: rehearsed breakfast, race vest, race shoes, race fueling cadence, run-everything execution. SPEC SOURCE: Race_Strategy_Response_v1 Answer B1 — the spec is a DISTRIBUTION, not an average; 130 ft/mi was never the problem and 172 was never the answer. ROUTE CONSTRAINT (non-negotiable): all added or steepened descent must be runnable (<10%); the technical-descent ban stands. Added climbing on a loop means added descending — route selection must absorb it at runnable grades. GATE CONDITION: this spec is conditional on Gate 2 (8/27) passing unflagged AND the 8/30 calibration reading clean. If either flags, this session REVERTS to 20 mi / 2,600 ft / 130 ft/mi and the spec is dropped without discussion — a gentler rehearsal is a smaller loss than a re-injury six days before taper. The revert is also guard-safe: 3,700 ft for the week is a decrease from W6.
